method: All PDF pages were reviewed through 4x4 contact sheets, with source-page fallback when a thumbnail was insufficient.
findings: Main-body completeness must be judged separately from code and data appendices.
A geometry or mechanism figure earns space only when it exposes objects, directions, boundaries, coordinates, or a decision criterion used by the mathematics.
Tables are the preferred carrier for exact plans and numeric decisions; prose should interpret only decisive differences.
Repeated curves, generic three-dimensional surfaces, software screenshots, and decorative workflows do not add evidence by themselves.
Small multiples are useful only when scale, encoding, panel labels, and comparison order remain readable at final LaTeX size.
A common useful data-paper sequence is data structure and quality, then diagnostics and uncertainty, then decision results.
Frequency in winning papers is descriptive evidence, not a contest requirement or proof of award causality.
limitations: The sample is not the complete population of awarded papers.
Page-level visual review does not prove formulas, exact numbers, table cells, or code correctness.
OCR-derived question boundaries are navigation aids and require semantic comparison with the original prompt.
